record_audits.database_subject: Cliotide U1, a Novel Antimicrobial Peptide Isolated From Urtica Dioica Leaves
record_audits.database_measure: Discovery: Purified by (NH4)2SO4 precipitation and chromatographic methods. Sequence analysis: APD analysis reveals that this sequence is similar (40%) to Cliotide T10. A: 20%, L: 17%, V=K: 11%. GRAVY: 0.87, mol Wt: 3995.89; mol formula: C193H315N46O44; mol ex coeff: 10020. Activity: active against E. coli ATCC 25922 (MIC 1 uM), S. aureus ATCC 25923 (MIC 4 uM), A. baumannii ATCC 19606 (MIC 2 ug/ml), and P. aeruginosa ATCC 27853 (MIC 1 uM). MBC was 2-fold higher. Peptide stability: not heat stable at 90oC treatment for 1 h. Antimicrobial robustness: activity is lost at pH 2-5. pH-senstive to acidic conditions. activity is human serum-sensitive (25%). In vitro toxicity: human RBC: 18% lysis at 32 uM. HEK293 cells: 94% alive treated at 1-4 uM. Structure: predicted to be helical.

sequence_check.modification_check: No modification evidence found in reopened XML/PDF/OA package.

record_audits.review_notes: APD6 free-text row is largely source-consistent for identity, DOI/PMID, sequence, activity pattern, hemolysis, and HEK293 viability, but it contains summary-level conflicts: A. baumannii MIC is expressed as ug/ml rather than source-supported uM, MBC is generalized as two-fold higher although one Table 3 row is four-fold, and some toxicity values are rounded. Preserved as source_conflict rather than normalized to source_verified.
